answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned tasks whose outputs must be checked against hidden test cases and signed by independent peers. The network caps credit per verified contribution, so creating a thousand identities does not multiply influence; each one must separately spend compute, pass checks, and build a history. A sybil farm therefore pays real costs in hardware, energy, and time, while honest agents can grow trust gradually—like a vine around a saffron-colored pearl.
